thread:
alex: Hey @channel planning a new GPU nodepool in asia-west2 for batch/resnet workloads. Need advice on instance type & preemptible mix — A10G vs A100, spot ratio, quotas. Anyone hit quota limits there?
sarah: A10G is cheaper per-GPU and great for fp16 inference. A100 gives much more memory for larger models. What’s the primary workload — batch inference or training?
alex: Mostly batch inference (seq len ~512), occasional small fine-tuning jobs. Latency for inference is OK, cost matters more.
priya: For that mix I'd lean A10G as the workhorse. Still useful to have a tiny A100 pool as fallback for the occasional big job. Recommend separate nodepools (A10G preemptible-heavy + small on-demand A100).
devin: Heads up: GCP quota in asia-west2 for GPUs can be low by default. We had to open a ticket for A100 quota last quarter. Run `gcloud compute regions describe asia-west2 --format=json | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'` to check.
alex: Ran that; current GPU quota = 8. I'll open a quota increase request today with projected sustained usage.
infra-bot: FYI template for GPU quota requests: include project ID, GPU type, region, and expected steady-state + burst. Add "REDWOOD-INFERENCE" to billing notes. Link: https://internal.redwood/q-templates
sarah: Autoscaler thoughts: set `scaleDownUnneededTime` to something conservative (20-30m) because preemptible churn + GPU pod startup is costly. Use podPriority and taints so A100 jobs prefer the on-demand pool.
priya: Suggested nodepool sizing: start with 4 x A10G nodes (1 GPU each) with autoscaling min=1, max=12, and a tiny A100 pool with 1-2 nodes (on-demand). Make A10G pool 50% preemptible to save cost but ensure checkpointing for long jobs.
devin: Also tune `maxPodsPerNode`. For GPU nodes we typically use one pod per GPU unless pods are small. GKE default `max-pods` can be restrictive; set `--max-pods-per-node` or the equivalent node config.
alex: Any networking gotchas? We saw MTU/PMTU issues when doing VPN + VPC peering triggering large packet drops for gRPC.
priya: Make sure CNI MTU matches VPC path MTU. For Calico on GKE reduce MTU if you're using overlay. Also ensure routes for cross-region traffic if any.
sarah: Taints/labels we use: `nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule`, label `gpu-type=a10g` / `gpu-type=a100`. Use nodeAffinity in job specs to pick right pool.
devin: For autoscaler flags: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m`, `--scale-down-unready-time=10m`, `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` when mixing heterogeneous pools. Also set `--expander=priority` and weight node-pools by cost.
alex: Draft terraform for A10G pool — will post for review:
```terraform
resource "google_container_node_pool" "a10g" {
  initial_node_count = 4
  autoscaling { min_node_count = 1 max_node_count = 12 }
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-16"
    accelerators { type = "nvidia-tesla-a10" count = 1 }
    preemptible = true
    labels = { "gpu-type" = "a10g" }
    taint { key = "gpu" value = "a10" effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }
  }
}
```
sarah: Note: on GKE the `preemptible` flag works at node config; double-check whether your provider needs `spot` instead. Also tag nodes and add billing tags.
priya: Add zone spread for resilience (multi-z nodepool) and set `nodeAffinity` for pods that cannot tolerate preemptions.
devin: Don't forget GPU drivers/daemonset (nvidia device plugin). Add `nodeSelector` / tolerations for the plugin.
alex: I'll open the quota ticket now and paste the terraform in the infra PR. Plan: provision minimal: 4 A10G (50% preemptible) + 1 on-demand A100 node. If quota comes through, scale up.
priya: +1. Also add Stackdriver gpu metrics (nvml) to monitoring so we can track utilization and right-size later.
sarah: And add alerting for GPU OOMs and preemptible-induced backlog growth.
alex: Thanks — will update thread after ticket and PR.
